metaDescription: Free online cURL command builder. Set method, URL, headers, body, auth and flags and get a correctly quoted curl command for your terminal.
intro: Fill in the method, URL, headers, body, authentication and flags to get a correctly quoted curl command. It can output one line or a multi-line command with backslashes.
why:
curl commands are the lingua franca for testing APIs, but quoting JSON bodies in a shell is easy to get wrong, and the flags are hard to remember. Single quotes inside a body, a missing header colon or a stray space can ruin a request.

Enter the method and URL, list headers as Name: value lines and paste the body in its own box. Pick bearer or basic authentication and flags for following redirects, silent mode, response headers, compression, failing on HTTP errors and a timeout. The tool escapes quotes properly and uses --data-raw so the body is sent as written. Avoid putting a real production token into a page you do not trust; this one runs in your browser and sends nothing. To go the other way, use cURL to Code.
howTo: Choose the method and enter the full URL starting with http or https.
Add headers as Name: value lines and paste the request body if there is one.
Select authentication and flags such as -L, -sS, --compressed or a timeout.
Copy the command, optionally as a multi-line version with backslashes.

faq.a: With --data-raw, which sends the text exactly as typed without treating @ as a file reference. The body is quoted safely for the shell, including any single quotes inside it.
It turns off TLS certificate checking. It is useful for testing local servers with self-signed certificates, but never use it against real services, as it removes protection against interception.

faq.q: How do I send basic authentication?
faq.a: Choose basic and enter user:password. The command gets a -u option. For bearer tokens, enter the token and an Authorization header is added.

faq.q: Can I convert a curl command into code?
faq.a: Yes, with the cURL to Code tool, which produces fetch, Node, Python or PHP code from a command.
